title: A specified 30-day activity filter leaves 3.3 to 6.3 percent of trial orbit amplitudes in 196 Gl 229 visits
abstract: We test a specified Gaussian-process activity filter on 196 public Gl 229 HARPS line-by-line visits. With a 30-day recurrence, 24-day coherence length and 2.5 m/s noise amplitude, subtraction leaves 3.3 to 6.3 percent of injected circular orbit amplitudes at 121.933, 471 and 523 days. A joint fit retains information but needs 2.04 to 2.81 m/s for 90 percent Gaussian power at a 1 percent fixed-period false alarm rate. Direct injections and 30000 simulated records check the calculations. None of three primary measured-velocity tests passes a 1 percent threshold corrected for three periods. The 122-day conditional tail changes greatly with the assumed coherence length. These are sensitivity results for fixed covariances, not measured planet limits or a reconstruction of the published activity fit. No new planet or physical cause is found. Independent observations, raw spectra, annual instrument controls and covariance inference remain needed. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes, an original figure and external retrieval steps are included. External observation records are excluded.

display.caption: Specified GP filtering reduces injected orbit amplitudes. Joint Gaussian power depends on coherence length. Solid and dashed lines give phase extrema. These are conditional model results.
